Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and the usage file. Really glad the recommendation feature is driving value.

High level we can do either a staged uplift (month-by-month buckets for Sep–Nov) or a single mid-contract uplift that folds into the renewal. Tradeoffs: staged gives you lower upfront cash outlay and smoother unit-price improvement; single uplift simplifies billing and gets you the best blended discount.

I’ll put together two concrete proposals with pricing and payment terms. Before I do: can you confirm if Procurement prefers invoices to come monthly or as a single amended invoice? Also, do you need an SOW scoped for the uplift (e.g., committed capacity + priority support)?

I’m looping in Jordan for billing cadence and Karthik for any technical guardrails if we need to pin model variants (to keep costs predictable).

Subject: Internal: Codelink uplift — pricing recommendation request

Team — quick ask. Codelink (DL-2026-0873) is up ~45% usage and wants a mid-contract uplift for Sep–Nov and to align renewal timing with Jan 31. Current ARR: $320k; expected uplift is ~+$85k over the 3-month period. They’re price sensitive and prefer smoother invoicing. Proposed options I’m drafting for them:

Option 1 (staged buckets): 3-month staged top-up (Sep/Oct/Nov) with a blended 8% discount on the uplifted units, monthly invoices for added buckets. Pros: lower cash hit; quicker to sign. Cons: slightly higher unit price.

Option 2 (one-time mid-contract uplift): Single uplift invoice now for the three months, 10% discount on uplift, and alignment to Jan 31 co-term (adjusts overall renewal pro-rate). Pros: best unit economics; cleaner accounting. Cons: larger upfront payment.

Requesting approval on the discount band (8% vs 10%) and guidance on whether we can offer net-60 on Option 2 for their procurement preference. Also asking for legal / SOW template — Marissa, can you prepare SOW_v2 if we go Option 2?

Karthik — any technical constraints on pinning model variants for a short uplift window (we may want to lock to an L2 quantized variant to ensure latency/SLOs during the spike)?

If we agree, I’ll send both options to Asha with the proposal PDF and SOW.

Thanks — Soojin

Hi Asha (and procurement team),

Thanks for the quick responses and for confirming you prefer monthly invoices for added capacity. Per our internal sync, please find two paths below and attached a short proposal + SOW for your review (attached: Codelink_Renewal_Proposal_Aug2026.pdf, SOW_Codelink_v2.docx).

Summary (two options):

1) Staged top-up (recommended if you want minimal cash flow impact)
   - Sep / Oct / Nov buckets: add X token units each month
   - Pricing: uplift units at a blended 8% discount vs current list unit price
   - Billing: monthly invoices for each bucket, no change to Jan 31 renewal
   - Turnaround: sign the attached SOW; we can activate within 3 business days of signature
2) Single mid-contract uplift + co-term to Jan 31 (recommended if you want the best unit economics)
   - One invoice today covering Sep–Nov uplift + co-term adjustment to align renewal
   - Pricing: uplift units at 10% discount; we can offer net-60 payment terms for this one-time invoice
   - Billing: one amended invoice and a single SOW addendum to be signed
Notes:
- We’ll pin the workload to the L2 quantized variant during the uplift window to keep latency consistent; Karthik is CC’d to coordinate.
- If procurement needs a PO number or specific billing language, please send that back and Jordan will add it to the invoice.

Next steps: please review the attached proposal and SOW and tell us which option you prefer. If Option 2 is chosen, confirm PO and whether net-60 is acceptable. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow to walk through either option.

Best,
